Assert that spells do not overlap within a unit

Source: R/expect_no_overlap.R
expect_no_overlap.Rd

A checkpoint for spell data, the other common shape of register data: address periods, employment spells, benefit periods. Each unit can only be in one spell at a time, so two spells for the same person that share a day are an error. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

expect_no_overlap(
  data,
  id,
  start,
  end,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL,
  log = getOption("daos.check_log"),
  dump = getOption("daos.check_dump")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

start, end

Columns with the first and last period of each spell (dates, or integers such as years).

success_msg

Message shown (and logged) when data is empty. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the log names every check that ran, and "The dataset is empty." otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown (and logged) when spells overlap and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when data is not empty. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

log

Optional path to a log file. The directory is created automatically. Defaults to getOption("daos.check_log").

dump

Optional directory. When the check fails, the offending rows are written there as a timestamped CSV file (UTF-8 with BOM, so Excel reads æøå correctly). Defaults to getOption("daos.check_dump").

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

On failure the overlapping spells are reported with an overlap_id column prepended, in the spirit of dupid in flag_duplicates(): spells that overlap each other (directly or through a chain) share an id, so each conflict can be inspected as a group.

Spells are treated as closed intervals, as register dates usually are: a spell ending 31 January and one starting 1 February do not overlap, while one ending and one starting on 1 February do. A missing end means an ongoing spell and overlaps everything after its start. Rows with a missing start are ignored; check them with expect_none()(data, is.na(start)), and spells that end before they start with expect_none()(data, end < start).

See also

expect_balanced() for yearly panels, expect_empty().

Examples

addresses <- data.frame(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-06-01")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-12-31", NA,           "2020-06-30", "2021-12-31"))
)

# b has two addresses in June 2020
expect_no_overlap(addresses, cpr, start, end)
#> Warning: Overlapping spells per cpr
#> ℹ 2 rows found:
#>   overlap_id = 1, cpr = "b", start = 2020-01-01, end = 2020-06-30
#>   overlap_id = 1, cpr = "b", start = 2020-06-01, end = 2021-12-31
